result:
The proposed answer of -1 does not match the result I recall, so I reject it.

I am working from memory of the literature rather than a derivation. The known result for the largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk in four dimensions gives expected length n(log n)^{-1/3+o(1)}, which would make α = -1/3.

The proposed derivation is a heuristic. It assumes the loops destroying a given loop occur independently at each scale, each with a constant hazard rate. It also treats a loop's survival as depending only on its own length. In four dimensions, the intersections between a loop and larger loops are correlated across scales, so these assumptions are unjustified. The resulting exponent -1 is therefore unreliable.

VERDICT: REJECT
